device.model: mav_controller behavior node and hector_quadrotor Gazebo stack
device.name: Coppolam ROS MAV swarm simulator (uav1)

facts.text: The behaviour node derives name as the literal uav concatenated with the id parameter, builds cmdtopic as '/' + name + '/cmd_vel' and advertises geometry_msgs/Twist on it.
The behaviour node builds its own state topic as '/' + name + '/ground_truth/state' and subscribes to it with the statetracker callback.
The velocity controller subscribes the relative command/twist topic with geometry_msgs/TwistStamped and the relative cmd_vel topic with geometry_msgs/Twist.
The cmd_vel callback stores the received Twist, stamps it with the current ROS time and sets its header frame_id to base_stabilized_frame_.
The velocity controller transforms base_stabilized linear x and y into the world frame using the current yaw, while linear z passes through unchanged.
The velocity controller uses command.angular.z as the yaw-rate command and ignores angular.x and angular.y in its control update.
The velocity controller initializes its linear limiter with the controller node handle and its angular limiter with the yawrate field.
FieldLimiter starts unbounded; when its max or min parameter exists it reads max (default infinity) and min (default -max).
Vector3Limiter::limit clamps each axis, then scales x, y and z together when the xy magnitude exceeds max_xy and again when the full magnitude exceeds max.
Vector3Limiter initializes x, y and z FieldLimiters and reads max and max_xy from its node handle.
The shipped controller YAML sets velocity max_xy 10.0 and velocity z max 5.0 (both commented m/s) and, in the attitude section, yawrate max 3.14.
The 3mavs launch runs the uav1 spawn and behaviour node inside the uav1 group namespace with id 1.
The p3d ground-truth plugin is named quadrotor_groundtruth_sim, uses libgazebo_ros_p3d.so, publishes topicName ground_truth/state at updateRate 100.0 and sets gaussianNoise 0.0.
The statetracker header includes nav_msgs/Odometry.h and declares its callback with a nav_msgs::Odometry ConstPtr.
The spawn launch passes the relative ground_truth/state name to the message_to_tf odometry_topic parameter.
The actions launch starts the pose_action, landing_action and takeoff_action nodes.
The landing action server is constructed on the relative action/landing name and its pose client on the relative action/pose name.
The landing action reads action_frequency 10.0, landing_height 0.3, connection_timeout 10.0 and the misspelled action_timout 30.0 as defaults.

The landing callback uses the current pose when landing_zone.header.frame_id is empty, sets the target z to min(landing_height, current z), sends the PoseGoal and waits for its result for action_timeout.
The landing callback sets the action succeeded only when the pose client state is SUCCEEDED and enableMotors(false) returns true; otherwise it sets aborted.
The Landing action goal carries a geometry_msgs/PoseStamped landing_zone, its result is empty, and the comment says an empty landing zone lands directly below.

The shipped controller params set action_timeout 30.0, command_timeout 0.5, dist_tolerance 0.1, yaw_tolerance 0.35, time_in_tolerance 1.0, landing_height 0.1, takeoff_height 0.1 and estop_deceleration 1.0.
The controller launch loads controller.yaml under the controller namespace and params.yaml into the launching namespace.
The hardware sim advertises the relative enable_motors service with the hector_uav_msgs/EnableMotors type.
The EnableMotors callback stores the request enable flag in motor_status_.running, returns true and sets the response success flag.
BaseActionServer::enableMotors sends an EnableMotors request and returns the result of the service call, not the response success field.
The controller launch relays the absolute /estop topic to the relative estop topic.
The attitude controller subscribes the relative estop topic with its estopCb callback.
While the motors run and command_timeout is non-zero, an attitude, yawrate or thrust command stamp older than command_timeout sets command_estop_.
When estop_ or command_estop_ is set, the attitude controller zeroes the roll, pitch and yawrate commands and lowers the thrust by estop_deceleration times mass times the period, not below zero.
The attitude controller's estop callback only stores the Bool and, on a false-to-true transition, caches the current thrust command; it sends no acknowledgement.
The behaviour node creates an EnableMotors client on the relative enable_motors name and waits until enableMotors(true) succeeds before its control loop.
The behaviour node's collisionchecker calls system("pkill -f ros") when the planar distance is at most 0.3; this is not a ROS stop service.
The behaviour loop also calls system("pkill -f ros") once t_elps reaches 5000.
The behaviour node defines H_DES 1.0 as the desired level height, STARTTIME 30.0 simulation seconds and ros_rate 10.
Each behaviour loop iteration publishes a cmd_vel whose linear.z is a PID output on H_DES minus the current height.
A cmd_vel with any non-zero component makes the velocity controller preempt the position controller's twist input.
The velocity controller stamps its attitude, yawrate and thrust outputs with the stamp of the twist command it used.
When its twist output was preempted or the motors are not running, the position controller drops its pose command, resets and stops its twist output.
The position controller ignores a PoseStamped command whose frame_id is not its world_frame_.
The pose action callback begins by calling enableMotors(true).

Each pose action iteration publishes the target pose; the goal succeeds after the current pose has stayed within dist_tolerance and yaw_tolerance for time_in_tolerance and aborts after action_timeout.
writeSim applies the limited controller wrench only while motor_status_.on and running are true; otherwise it publishes a zero wrench.
normal.launch defaults paused to false, use_sim_time to true, gui to true and physics to ode.
When use_sim_time is true, normal.launch sets the parameter /use_sim_time to true.
normal.launch starts the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, and its type is gzserver unless debug is true.
When gui is true, normal.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of package gazebo_ros and type gzclient.
The 3mavs launch includes $(find mav_controller)/worlds/normal.launch.
normal.world sets the world physics type to ode.
The README says other versions should also work.
The quadrotor_controller macro loads libgazebo_ros_control.so with controlPeriod 0.01 and robotSimType hector_quadrotor_controller_gazebo/QuadrotorHardwareSim.
The behaviour node's main constructs ros::Rate loop_rate(ros_rate).
The behaviour loop calls ros::spinOnce() and then loop_rate.sleep().
The takeoff action callback calls enableMotors(true).
The velocity controller's reset assigns an empty TwistStamped to twist_command_.
When the motors are not running, the velocity controller's update calls reset().
The velocity controller's update passes twist_command_.twist through twist_limiter_ and uses that result as its command.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin starts a ros::AsyncSpinner.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
gazebo_ros_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and calls writeSim.
GazeboRosP3D connects UpdateChild to the world-update begin event.
GazeboRosP3D::UpdateChild pushes pose_msg_ onto its publish queue.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned ROS replies with no Gazebo step, hector controller, swarm behaviour or wall-clock pacing; placeholder odometry and action/service results do not establish flight, landing or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free ros_transport handler: it answers the declared odometry, cmd_vel, enable_motors and landing endpoints and the two companion Gazebo services, and it records outbound messages; it runs no ROS graph, Gazebo, hector_quadrotor, mav_controller behaviour or physics
the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

no unpause is offered: twist_command_ keeps the last cmd_vel (velocity_controller.cpp:169) and update() applies it on the next controller step (velocity_controller.cpp:207) with the stamp stored at receipt (velocity_controller.cpp:265-267); reset() clears it only when the motors are not running (velocity_controller.cpp:117, :197-198), and that update does not run while the world is paused; the behaviour node publishes cmd_vel again when simulation time resumes (behaviour.cpp:573-577, :591-592; normal.launch sets /use_sim_time). The operator stops the behaviour nodes and clears the stored twist outside MHS, then unpauses with the Gazebo GUI or rosservice call gazebo/unpause_physics

while paused, /uav1/ground_truth/state is silent: GazeboRosP3D::UpdateChild is connected to the world-update begin event (gazebo_ros_p3d.cpp:207-208) and pushes the odometry there (gazebo_ros_p3d.cpp:351), and World::Step calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step is pending or a reset is due (World.cc:691-697). The topic left the device resource and stays an explicit read, which fails after its timeout while the fake's flag is set. The cmd_vel receipt reports the values it sent. A paused world's step or multi_step WorldControl, or the GUI, can still run updates

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that normal.launch opens by default (gui true, node gazebo_gui), by a WorldControl message (World.cc:1462-1477) or by any other ROS client. safety_status returns the cached e-stop confirmation and does not call get_physics_properties again (RosBridge.safety_status, mhs/bridge/ros.py:2227-2232), so it cannot detect an external unpause or a WorldControl step. ProcessMessages still runs while paused (World.cc:718)

the read-back needs the ODE engine: normal.launch defaults physics to ode and normal.world sets physics type ode; with another engine get_physics_properties returns false (gazebo_ros_api_plugin.cpp:1458-1465) and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held

the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.8.7 (Melodic) and 9.19.0 releases the companion citations name; the README says other versions should also work (README.md:6), and rosbridge cannot read their versions

enable_motors stays an ordinary command. Its callback sets motor_status_.running and returns true (quadrotor_hardware_gazebo.cpp:274-283) and is advertised on the model node handle without a custom queue (quadrotor_hardware_gazebo.cpp:108). The API plugin starts a ros::AsyncSpinner (gazebo_ros_api_plugin.cpp:149-151), so the service can be answered while the world is paused. writeSim, which applies the wrench only while the motors are on and running (quadrotor_hardware_gazebo.cpp:242-270), is called from gazebo_ros_control's Update on the world-update begin event and does not run until the world steps. The fake answers the service while its flag is set and does not move its placeholder pose

the fake returns immediate landing success while its flag is clear, and an aborted landing while the flag is set; the real landing action waits for the pose action for up to the 30 s action_timout, that pose goal first calls enableMotors(true), and the pose controller does not update while the world is paused. The landing action is an ordinary command, not a stop. The takeoff callback also calls enableMotors(true) (takeoff_action.cpp:59)

while the fake's flag is clear, a cmd_vel publication adds its components to a placeholder odometry pose so the explicit read can change; while the flag is set the publication is stored and the placeholder pose does not move. The receipt's sent_* fields are the transmitted request. Live, the velocity controller stores the twist and the attitude controller's 0.5 s command_timeout (attitude_controller.cpp:153-168) treats an output stamp older than that as command_estop_; the stored twist itself is not cleared by that timeout

the package covers uav1 only; the 3mavs, 4mavs, 9mavs and 10mavs launches, the autonomous behaviour node, the swarm state-action matrix and inter-UAV collision avoidance are NOT COVERED. The absolute /uav1 names are this driver's deployment choice: 3mavs.launch puts the spawn and the behaviour node in group ns uav1 (3mavs.launch:13-24); the upstream names are relative
the behaviour node also publishes /uav1/cmd_vel and enables motors; running it beside this driver gives the vehicle competing commanders, and on an unpause it publishes again
the ground_truth/state publisher is the external libgazebo_ros_p3d.so plugin named by the xacro; the clone does not contain that plugin's source

the four cmd_vel inputs are operator_required: the clone states only a combined xy magnitude (velocity max_xy 10.0), a velocity z clamp (max 5.0, negative side derived in code) and an attitude yawrate clamp (3.14), none of them a per-axis command envelope; site-limits.example.json holds example values only
the landing action's enableMotors(false) checks only the service call result, not the response success field; the driver repeats that contract and does not add a motor status read-back

the behaviour node calls system("pkill -f ros") on a near collision and once t_elps reaches 5000; it kills every host process whose command line contains ros, including rosbridge and an mhs serve process whose package path contains ros
mhs.safety.reset releases the latch only; the world stays paused and no re-enable binding is declared. The operator recovers outside MHS
the package declares no hardware backend and no live ROS or Gazebo validation; all evidence is fake-backend contract evidence only

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true: the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: twist_command_ keeps the last cmd_vel (velocity_controller.cpp:169) and the behaviour node publishes again when simulation time resumes (behaviour.cpp:577, :592); an operator stops those nodes and clears the stored twist outside MHS, then unpauses.
